elements.element: Customer has no non-compete or field-of-use restriction.
elements.evidence: Section 12.4, which had imposed a 24-month post-term restriction on Customer developing, marketing, selling, or acquiring "any product or service that competes with Vendor in any territory," is rendered as "[Intentionally omitted.]" Retained Section 12.3 affirmatively confirms nothing restricts Customer from developing, acquiring, licensing, selling, or using any product or service or conducting business in any field or territory, and that Customer has made no non-compete commitment. No other cited provision imposes a field-of-use or competitive restriction on Customer.

elements.element: The restriction covers only a named competing product.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no restriction on Customer survives after the deletion of Section 12.4, so there is no restriction whose scope could exceed a named competing product. The fallback narrowing is offered only in the margin comment, which is appropriate since the preferred level is achieved.

elements.element: The restriction applies during the term only.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the only term/post-term restriction (Section 12.4's "During the term and for twenty-four months thereafter") has been struck, leaving no operative restriction with any duration.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the 24-month tail is deleted; no residual duration mechanic remains in the rendered language.

elements.element: The restriction permits Customer's internal development.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply, and retained Section 12.3 expressly confirms nothing restricts Customer from developing any product or service.
Condition does not apply, and retained Section 12.3 expressly confirms nothing restricts Customer from acquiring any product or service.

reasons: Preferred level is complete: the single preferred element is met by striking Section 12.4 in full, and the surviving Section 12.3 confirmation leaves no non-compete or field-of-use restriction binding Customer.

Minimality holds: the edit touches only the offending sentence (deleting a sentence that is entirely the target restriction), retains the favourable Section 12.3 language untouched, and avoids restating the same permission a second time. Marking 12.4 as "[Intentionally omitted.]" preserves numbering and any cross-references to later sections.

Intent is preserved: the deletion creates no undefined term or dangling cross-reference, and it removes the contradiction between Section 12.4 and the pro-Customer confirmation in Section 12.3 rather than creating one. Section 13.4 use restrictions, Section 2.2 exclusivity (a separate rule), and Section 24.2 Vendor-side restrictions are left intact.

The narrowed fallback (named competing product, term only, 12-month cap, internal-development and acquisition carve-outs) is correctly offered in the margin comment rather than drafted into the operative text, which would have been non-minimal given the preferred position is achievable.
Deterministic checks corroborate substance: the operation applies, no open-ended compete restriction on Customer remains in the rendered text, and both the minimality and element-coverage gates pass.
